scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: When you supply to a money market, you're the bank's depositor, and effectively its credit desk. Your return: supply A.P.Y. about borrow A.P.Y. times utilisation times (1 minus reserve factor). Modern designs split lending into isolated markets (one collateral, one loan asset, one oracle, one liquidation L.T.V.). Curated vaults spread deposits across several of these; the curator decides the allocation. What a lender must check: Collateral quality and liquidation L.T.V.: the higher the L.T.V., the thinner the buffer before bad debt Oracle: what prices the collateral, and can it be manipulated? (Module 5.3) Utilisation: near 100% means you may not be able to withdraw Curator: track record, how allocations are changed, timelocks Risk-adjusted return, not headline
scenes.cap: Collateral quality and liquidation LTV: the higher the LTV, the thinner the buffer before bad debt Oracle: what prices the collateral, and can it be manipulated? scenes.vo: Vault A: 7% headline, exposure to newer collateral; you assume a 2% a year chance of a loss event losing half the deposit to 6.0% risk-adjusted. Vault B: 4.5% headline, blue-chip collateral; 0.5% a year, total loss assumed to 4.0%. the calculator A pays more after the haircut, if your loss estimates are honest. Split between them, and cap A lower because its tail is fatter and less known.

lines: Borrow APY 10%, utilisation 70%, reserve factor 10%. Supply APY?
scenes.vo: Borrow A.P.Y. 10%, utilisation 70%, reserve factor 10%. Supply A.P.Y.? ... Pause and think. ... The answer: 6.3%.

lines: Why is utilisation at 100% a lender's problem?
scenes.sub: Answer: All liquidity is lent out, so withdrawals wait until borrowers repay or new deposits arrive.

lines: What's a curated vault's extra risk?
scenes.sub: Answer: The curator's allocation decisions and permissions, on top of each market's risk.
